# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background; call `activate_tab(target)` only when the user explicitly asks
  or a page demonstrably pauses rendering while hidden.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.

  - `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs:1465` (LlmAgent streaming loop). It calls `acc.observe(&ev)` at :1469 and `acc.finish()` at :1505. Then `conversation.extend(items.iter().cloned())` at ~:1514.
  - `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/activities.rs:98` (durable model activity). It calls `acc.observe` and `acc.finish()` and wraps the result in `ModelTurnResult`.
  - Provider tests and live round trips use it only as a helper: `providers-anthropic/src/translate/mod.rs:990` (`items_of`), `providers-anthropic/src/live_round_trip.rs:137`, `providers-gemini/src/translate/mod.rs:369`, `providers-gemini/src/live_round_trip.rs:52` and `providers-litellm/src/stream.rs:852`.
- No separate non-streaming path and no `collect` assembly from ModelEvents. `RunResultStreaming::collect` and `collect_typed` work on `AgentEvent::MessageOutput` items that already exist. They skip provider-data-only messages (tests in `runner.rs` ~:1150-1200).
- Other `Item::AssistantMessage { content: vec![Text] }` constructions do not come from ModelEvents. They are `graph.rs:263/372-373` (final_text), `agent.rs:107/1720`, `workflow.rs:450`, `session.rs`, and `compacting_session.rs`.

**2. Text joining: ONE Text part per turn, no splitting signal.**
- `model.rs:701`: `ModelEvent::TokenDelta { text } => self.text.push_str(text),`
- Reasoning is the same: `ReasoningDelta` goes into `self.reasoning` at :702.
- `build_items` (:623-632) emits at most one `Reasoning` and one `Text`:
```rust
if !reasoning.is_empty() { content.push(ContentPart::Reasoning { text: reasoning }); }
if !text.is_empty()      { content.push(ContentPart::Text { text }); }
content.extend(provider_data);
```
- A turn therefore yields at most one `AssistantMessage`, with at most one `Reasoning` and one `Text`. Any interleaving of text and tool calls or provider data in the stream is lost.
- Nothing in the event set can split text.

**3. Order of parts in the content Vec**
- Fixed order: `[Reasoning?, Text?, ProviderData*...]`.
- `ToolUse` is never produced by the accumulator. Tool calls become separate top-level `Item::ToolCall`s that follow the message, in `BTreeMap` order, so sorted by `call_id` (`build_items` :634-656; `ModelTurn.items` docs at :572-577).
- `ProviderData` parts are pushed in `observe` at :738-745 in arrival order among themselves. They are always placed after Reasoning and Text, regardless of where they arrived in the stream.
- The test `provider_data_follows_reasoning_and_text` (~:879) feeds `PD(None,1)`, Reasoning, Text, `PD(Some("x"),2)` and asserts `[Reasoning, Text, PD idx1, PD idx2]`.
- Message creation condition (:622): `!text.is_empty() || !reasoning.is_empty() || !provider_data.is_empty()`. A tool-only turn with provider data gets an `AssistantMessage` holding only ProviderData, before the `ToolCall` items (test `tool_only_turn_with_provider_data_gets_assistant_message`, ~:845).

**4. `ModelEvent` enum:** `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:253`, `#[non_exhaustive]`. The variants are:
- `TokenDelta { text }` (:255)
- `ReasoningDelta { text }`
- `ToolCallDelta { call_id, name: Option<String>, args_delta }`
- `Usage { input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens, reasoning_tokens }`
- `ProviderData { provider, call_id: Option<String>, data: serde_json::Value }` (:334)
- `Finish { reason: FinishReason }`

There is no text block start/stop, part boundary, or index variant.

**5. ProviderData with and without `call_id`:** handled identically.
- `observe` (:738-745) pushes `ContentPart::ProviderData { provider, call_id: call_id.clone(), data }` to the same `provider_data` Vec. The `call_id` is only carried along.
- It is not tied to a ToolCall and is not reordered.
- `ContentPart::ProviderData` is at `item.rs:151`. Its doc (:139-142) says `call_id: Some(id)` means the data belongs to the tool call with that id in the same response, an `Item::ToolCall` following the message or a `ToolUse` in the same message.

**6. Contract statements**
- `model.rs:561-565` (`ModelTurn` doc): "the concatenated text/reasoning deltas become at most one [`Item::AssistantMessage`]. Provider data alone also creates that message."
- `model.rs:~582` (`ModelTurn.items` field doc): "an optional leading `AssistantMessage` (text, reasoning and/or provider data content, in that order) followed by zero or more `ToolCall`s, in deterministic `call_id`-sorted order."
- `item.rs:143-146` (`ContentPart::ProviderData` doc): "The position of the part in `content` has no meaning. `ProviderData` parts keep their arrival order among themselves. A provider that needs block structure stores the whole block in `data`."
- `model.rs:329-333` (`ModelEvent::ProviderData` doc): "The position of the event in the stream has no meaning."
- Tests: `accumulates_text_reasoning_and_tool_calls` (`model.rs:803`). It feeds two TokenDeltas ("hel","lo") and expects `items.len() == 2`, i.e. one AssistantMessage (reasoning+text) and one ToolCall.
- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/provider_data_text_guard.rs` (SMA-827) checks that provider-data-only messages are invisible to text consumers. `Item::is_provider_data_only` is at `item.rs:~64-79`.
- No doc or test states a strict "exactly one Text part" invariant beyond the "at most one AssistantMessage" wording above.
